key_insight: LLM-simulated counselling clients showed both similarities and differences to human role-players in communication patterns, suggesting potential for training support rather than demonstrated equivalence.
engineering_relevance: LLM-based client simulations could expand counselling practice opportunities, but should be evaluated for realistic dialogue and their effects on trainee behaviour.
method: Recorded novice counsellors role-playing with human peers as clients.
Conducted human–AI role-plays using Mixtral 8x7B with 4-bit quantization.
Analysed sentence-level counselling patterns to compare dialogue dynamics and counsellor behaviour.
evidence_signal: Sentence-level analysis found similarities and differences across human-client and LLM-client sessions; the abstract reports no sample sizes or quantitative effect estimates.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether practising with simulated clients improves counselling skills or transfers to real-client interactions.
paper_title: Comparing Human Role-Players and LLM-Simulated Clients in Online Counselling Training: An Analysis of Counselling Patterns
